label: The unfinished first piece of a word that the next token must complete. Strongest: the katakana long mark ー fused with a raw byte of the next kana (as in ハーバー, オーディオ, ハーブ, ブーツ). Weaker: a short word-start piece split off a longer word, such as a lone capital in an abbreviation or caps heading (U|ds., E|COLOGY), French retr|ouvent, Arabic السي|ّد. Quiet for words kept as whole tokens, including katakana like ジーンズ or ヒーロー, and ordinary lowercase English words; a space before a rare symbol (☃, ♞) fires only weakly, inside mixed-script text.
